summary: Validates texture surface parameters against fixed limits (dimensions <= 65500, sub-surface count <= 10, pixel format == 8, per-descriptor factor pair within [1,4]), reporting each failure through the object's vtable callback while continuing execution. Then runs two passes over the sub-surface descriptor array at this+0xC4 (84-byte stride): the first accumulates maximum width/height factors into this+0x10C/0x110, the second computes each descriptor's aligned dimensions and strides via CeilingDivision against those maxima. Finally refreshes the output surface active flag at *(this+0x18C)+0x10 when the output surface count is stale or the this+0xC8 flag is set.

local_names.obj: *(this+0): object whose vtable reports validation errors

operations.description: If texture total width (this+0x18) or total height (this+0x1C) exceeds 65500, proceed to report the oversized dimension.
Set error code slot obj+0x14 (obj = *(this+0)) to 40 for an oversized texture dimension.
Set error detail slot obj+0x18 to 65500 (the dimension clamp limit).
Invoke the object's vtable callback through the pointer at this+0 to report the dimension failure; execution continues after the call.
If expected pixel format (this+0xC0) is not 8, proceed to report the format mismatch.
Set error code slot obj+0x14 to 13 for the pixel format mismatch.
Set error detail slot obj+0x18 to the offending pixel format value (this+0xC0).
Invoke the object's vtable callback through the pointer at this+0 to report the format failure.
If sub-surface count (this+0x20) exceeds 10, proceed to report the oversized count.
Set error code slot obj+0x14 to 24 for the oversized sub-surface count.
Set error detail slot obj+0x18 to the offending count (this+0x20).
Set error detail slot obj+0x1C to 10 (the accepted count limit).
Invoke the object's vtable callback through the pointer at this+0 to report the count failure.
Initialize maximum width factor accumulator this+0x10C to 1.
Initialize maximum height factor accumulator this+0x110 to 1.
First pass: loop over the first this+0x20 descriptors of the array at this+0xC4 (84-byte stride), skipping entirely when the count is <= 0.
If the sub-surface height factor (*(this+0xC4)+0xC; the width factor at +8 is checked the same way) is not within [1,4], proceed to report a factor validation failure.
Set error code slot obj+0x14 to 16 for an out-of-range factor.
Invoke the object's vtable callback through the pointer at this+0 to report the factor failure; the loop continues.
Accumulate this+0x10C as the maximum width factor seen across descriptors.
Accumulate this+0x110 as the maximum height factor seen across descriptors.
Set shared output pixel format this+0x114 to 8.

Second pass: loop over the first this+0x20 descriptors of the array at this+0xC4 (84-byte stride), skipping entirely when the count is <= 0, computing per-descriptor aligned dimensions, strides and flags.
Set each sub-surface descriptor pixel format (*(this+0xC4)+0x24) to 8.
Compute aligned width *(this+0xC4)+0x1C = CeilingDivision(total width * width factor, 8 * max width factor).
Compute aligned height *(this+0xC4)+0x20 = CeilingDivision(total height * height factor, 8 * max height factor).
Compute padded stride width *(this+0xC4)+0x28 = CeilingDivision(total width * width factor, max width factor).
Compute padded stride height *(this+0xC4)+0x2C = CeilingDivision(total height * height factor, max height factor).
Clear the descriptor dirty/modified flag *(this+0xC4)+0x4C to 0.
Set the descriptor stride-valid flag byte *(this+0xC4)+0x30 to 1.
Compute this+0x118 = CeilingDivision(total height, 8 * max height factor).
If tracked output surface count (this+0x120) is less than the sub-surface count (this+0x20), or the byte flag at this+0xC8 is non-zero, mark the output surface state for refresh.
Set the output surface active flag byte *(this+0x18C)+0x10 to 1 (needs refresh).
Else, clear the output surface active flag byte *(this+0x18C)+0x10 to 0.
Return the output surface state pointer (this+0x18C).
